column1: # Clause dispositions: authored input to the ECMA-262 census.
# Three tab-separated fields: <clause id> <kind or *> <disposition>. The
# section key is a clause id, resolved by the innermost enclosing clause of the
# row's span, with a kind-specific line preferred to the clause's wildcard
# line. Duplicate (clause, kind) fails; an unknown kind or disposition fails;
# an entry no row uses fails; a row no entry reaches fails.
# Every line below is keyed on the row's OWN innermost enclosing clause, so the
# join needs no outward walk and gives the same answer if it does one. That
# costs fifty-two lines instead of a dozen and buys a table a reviewer can read
# against the ECMA-262 section table of SPEC-MANIFEST.md row by row.
# Seeded from that table as amended by ruling R-P5, whose one change to the
# survey's proposal is that HostEnqueuePromiseJob and its ordering bullet are
# `requirement`, realized by the FIFO queue in `Whatwg.Ecma262.Jobs` under
# DB-03, the same specification/realizer pattern as ReadableStreamPipeTo.
# HostEnqueueTimeoutJob and HostEnqueueGenericJob stay `foreignBoundary`, and
# the five promise instance slots are `owned` here while the Streams census
# keeps the same named slots `foreignBoundary`: the two censuses answer two
# ownership questions about two libraries.
# These are proposals until the coordinator ratifies them; nothing here is
# coverage. Section 6 of test/contracts/ecma262-census.contract.md freezes the
# totals they must produce: owned 44, foreignBoundary 13, hostOnly 10,
# requirement 7, evidenceOnly 3, denominator 74 of 77 rows.
# --- 9.5 Jobs and Host Operations to Enqueue Jobs ---------------------------
# The clause's own text is the four host job-scheduling requirements; DB-03's
# FIFO queue is their realizer. The three terms it defines are split: `job` is
# the carrier, the other two are defined over the execution context stack.
sec-jobs
sec-jobs
# The JobCallback Record exists only to carry a host-defined value across a job
# boundary. Its [[Callback]] field is owned; see overrides.tsv.
sec-jobcallback-records
sec-jobcallback-records
# Two hooks whose whole purpose is attaching host state and re-entering user
# code, with the one requirement bullet each states.
sec-hostmakejobcallback
sec-hostcalljobcallback
# No in-scope algorithm calls this hook; it is out of the promise lane.
sec-hostenqueuegenericjob
# R-P5: the hook is a specification realized by the FIFO queue. Its realm and
# active-script bullets are host bookkeeping the model never observes; the
# ordering bullet is the DB-03 sentence and is overridden below.
sec-hostenqueuepromisejob
sec-hostenqueuepromisejob
# Wall-clock scheduling; "at least _milliseconds_ milliseconds" is not FIFO
# state and nothing in the promise lane calls it.
sec-hostenqueuetimeoutjob
# The fulfilled/rejected/pending/settled/resolved vocabulary and two bare
# headings. R-P5 adopted the survey's `evidenceOnly` for all three; review debt
# D4, amendment 1.1 of test/contracts/ecma262-census-q2.contract.md,
# 2026-09-07, separates the one clause that carries text a declaration realizes
# from the two that carry none. The own prose of sec-promise-objects is the
# promise state vocabulary that Whatwg.Ecma262.Promise.State realizes under
# R-P13, so it is a row the model answers to and belongs in the denominator
# where a witness can be owed; owed is not held, and the row stays absent.
# Its two siblings are bare headings whose own prose is a section title, and
# every operation under them is already its own row, so they stay evidenceOnly.
sec-promise-objects
sec-promise-abstract-operations
sec-promise-jobs
# DB-11 puts both records and every field in `Whatwg.Ecma262`.
sec-promisecapability-records
sec-promisereaction-records
# A shorthand whose explicit six-step expansion is the theorem.
sec-ifabruptrejectpromise
# First-order state transitions over the promise slots.
sec-createresolvingfunctions
sec-fulfillpromise
sec-newpromisecapability
sec-ispromise
sec-rejectpromise
sec-triggerpromisereactions
# Pure host bookkeeping; the default returns ~unused~ and the text states no
# observable effect.
sec-host-promise-rejection-tracker
# The two job constructors. The thenable `then` call of the second is a
# boundary step inside an owned row, not a boundary row.
sec-newpromisereactionjob
sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob
# Global-object plumbing: %Promise% as the initial value of the global
# property, [[Prototype]], and `extends`. The `%Promise%` term it defines is an
# intrinsic identity the host's realm supplies.
sec-promise-constructor
# Where a promise is created and CreateResolvingFunctions is called; the
# NewTarget and OrdinaryCreateFromConstructor steps are left to the host object
# model as dependency rows.
sec-promise-executor
sec-properties-of-the-promise-constructor
# The combinators and their Perform* operations: the whole combinator
# semantics, with the iterator protocol entering as an external.
sec-promise.all
sec-getpromiseresolve
sec-performpromiseall
sec-promise.allsettled
sec-performpromiseallsettled

# Property descriptors, and a species accessor whose only purpose is subclass
# dispatch enforced by the host object model.
sec-promise.prototype
sec-get-promise-%symbol.species%

sec-properties-of-the-promise-prototype-object
